steps.text: Whisk together eggs, milk, flour, melted butter, sugar, and salt in a large bowl until smooth.
Heat a medium skillet or crêpe pan over medium heat. Grease the pan with a small amount of butter or oil applied with a brush or paper towel.
Using a serving spoon or small ladle, spoon about 3 tablespoons crêpe batter onto the hot pan, tilting the pan to evenly coat the bottom surface.
Cook until golden brown, 1 to 2 minutes per side.

raw_recipe.headline: Dessert Crêpes
raw_recipe.description: This crêpe recipe is made with basic pantry staples and turns out perfectly delicate with crisp edges for a fancy breakfast or eye-catching dessert.

review.reviewBody: I had never made crepes before, but thought, "how hard could it be?" Well, it does take a little practice. The first few attempts were "practice crepes"! You need the right sized pan, and it should be nonstick, for ease of turning. A tiny bit of Pam sprayed on the pan ensures that they don't stick, and worked better for me than oil or butter. I kept trying to turn the crepe to soon, and it would fall apart. Go ahead and let it cook until it looks completely cooked before you flip it, and then it only has to cook for just a bit on the other side. I also found a fairly low heat works best - around 2 on my particular stove. We fill these with a mixture of warm sweetened cottage cheese and cream cheese flavored with a bit of vanilla, and then top with either a fresh fruit sauce or canned fruit filling. Cottage cheese gets very watery when warmed, so you either need to strain it before mixing with the other ingredients, or use dry curd cottage cheese. We have also slathered Nutella on the crepe, filled with sliced bananas, and topped with slivered almonds and whipped cream.

Tasted great! I added a fresh strawberry relish I made to the middle, rolled them, sprinkled powdered sugar on them & sprayed redi-whip on top.

I did find it hard to get thin crepes using a sm frying pan (because of the pan they were also harder to flip & they needed to be flipped because they weren't thin enough). 

I just ordered a crepe maker though because I liked the taste enough that I knew I could improve upon it & get perfection.

Love it! Made some for me & my son! So good! Wasn't feeling well. But success with these made my day! I have a granite nonstick pan. So great to make them! My son made a quick sweet sauce , Brown sugar ,cinnamon & butter. I also took frozen berries,sprinkled raw sugar & folded them into one!
So good! I am so glad I got this recipe!

It was a great recipe, easy to prepare, and cook. I even tried using half whole wheat, half all purpose flour, and it didn't effect the taste or texture at all. Great with peaches and whipped cream. In the recipe, it says to use a crepe pan, but a normal cast-iron pan is what I used, and it was very easy. And as a response to the review where someone asked if they can mix the batter, and leave it in the fridge, yes you can; I did it.
This was delicious and easy. I took a few tips from other reviewers that I plan to use again. I sifter the flour and blended all ingredients in the blender. Super smooth batter with minimal mess.

Make sure the butter (or coconut oil) is completely melted before mixing it in (I learned the hard way the first time). Also helps to sift the flour while adding. Add 1/4 teaspoon of vanilla if you like vanilla. Yum!
perfect every time. the trick to a lump free batter is to add the flour and eggs together first, then slowly add the milk in last.

Never made crepes before but now this is a breakfast fav at home. I add a little vanilla extract to the batter for more flavor.
 I cut strawberries and rub them with a little sugar and let them sit overnight in the fridge for filling.
 Add a little La Lachera condensed milk with the strawberries in the crepes and there won't be any left!

ALWAYS mix wet and dry ingredients separately and then when thats done, mix wet into dry. I did as recipe said and the end result was a clumpy mixture that the blender saved. The ingredients in the blender became a creamy tasty mixture.
Even the 9 month old baby ate the crepe. ;) I do love this flexible crepe recipe.
I add 2 extra eggs, vanilla, and cinnamon. Sauteed apples in butter are a great healthy filling.

Super tasty! I stuffed them with chocolate chips and marshmallows and topped with powdered sugar!! So easy to make and all I’m wondering is if I don’t use all the batter can I put in fridge for next day??

I don’t know how you got my Dutch Master Grandmother’s recipe for crepes, but you mastered it!! One caviet, she would dump the ingredients into a Mason jar, shake the Dickens out of it and put it into the fridge overnight before cooking the crepes. I’m 78 and had forgotten the ratios, they were most important to her and I now remember, thank you so very much!❤️

I halved the recipe, and it turned out great—everyone in the family loved it. It was my first time making crêpes; I did pour a bit too much batter, so the shape wasn't quite right and they looked more like pancakes, but I learned from that, and my subsequent crêpes turned out better. Thanks for the excellent tutorial! ❤️
I loved it but we added a ton of powdered sugar and it over powered it so word of advice dont add to much powdered sugar.
It was so yum! i made this for my sibling who have hated crepes before! and they loved it! 10 STARS ִֶָ 𓂃˖˳·˖ ִֶָ ⋆★⋆ ִֶָ˖·˳˖𓂃 ִֶָ
I've always been afraid to make crepes but this recipe was easy to follow. Crepes turned out perfectly and are delicious! My family thinks I'm a chef now! It's my go-to recipe!

This is ALL OF MY CHILDRENS FAVORITE BREAKFAST or Anytime meal honestly, with FRESH FRUIT mixed w a touch of brown sugar and a bit more sugar to the crepes, along with freshly made whipped cream, Nutella( kids) just a EASY GREAT FAMILY TREAT!!

My original review was lost when Allrecipes became MyRecipies. This is really good! I add a splash of vanilla and a dash of cinnamon per other reviews. I have not solved the issue of lumpy batter yet, but the lumps don't seem to affect the final product. I use 1/4 cup batter in a perfectly sized frying pan. I put out a bar of chocolate chips, Nutella, Fluff, blueberries, strawberries, chocolate syrup, whipped cream, sugar cinnamon and anything else on had or that grabs our fancy for fillings/toppings. The family loves.
